title: Astro Portal API v1 equipment
description: GET /v1/equipment response (packages/portal/src/persistence/equipment-reader.js). Device-bearer only, tenant-scoped to the authenticated device's owner; a paired device allowed to write also adds one item with POST /v1/equipment (the body and the answer of POST /v1/manage/equipment: manage-equipment.schema.json `equipmentInput` in `{ equipment }`, `item` with 201) — the same item shape the web planner's equipment endpoint returns. The schema adds, additively, `defaults` (the active « Matériel par défaut » every space is offered, without the organisation that holds it nor its notes) and `hideDefaultEquipment` (the space's option « Masquer le matériel par défaut »); a client reading an older portal finds neither. It also adds, additively, `defaultConfiguration`: « Ma configuration par défaut » of the space (`$defs/defaultConfiguration`, also the shape of GET /v1/manage/default-configuration), null when none is set.

planner.description: What the planners read of the item. Additive fields: on a filter `equipmentIds` (the ids of the telescopes and cameras it is attached to) and `forAllEquipment` (offered for all equipment, the default true; false limits it to `equipmentIds`); on a telescope or a camera `ownFiltersOnly` (offer only the filters attached to it, default false, true for a telescope made from a smart-telescope profile); on a telescope `profileId` (the id of the common profile it was made from, which names its built-in filters); on a telescope `finder` (`aligned`: its finder is aligned with the tube; `none`: no finder; absent: not said — what the phone's axis calibration asks first); on every item `maker` (the maker's name, as the pickers' « Marque » menu lists it) and `kind` (a telescope's optical formula `refractor`, `newtonian`, `schmidt-cassegrain`, `maksutov`, `ritchey-chretien`, `cassegrain` or `smart`; an eyepiece's `zoom`, `plossl`, `orthoscopic`, `standard`, `wide-field` or `ultra-wide-field`; a camera's `colour` or `mono`; a reducer or Barlow's `reducer`, `barlow` or `flattener`), each absent on a generic entry; on a mount that can flip (equatorial, hybrid, or a kind not said) `meridianLimitMinutes` (a whole number of minutes, 0 to 120, that the mount can keep tracking past the meridian before it flips; 0: it flips at the meridian; absent: not said, no cut; never written for an alt-az mount, a tracker or a smart telescope). On a guide scope (made on the phone, edited on the web with the same fields) `guideScope`: `telescopeId` (the telescope it rides on; absent: none), `placement` (`guide` or `main`), `camera` (`name`, `pixelSizeUm`, `widthPx`, `heightPx`, `sensor` `mono` or `colour`), `protocol` (`alpaca` or `indi`), (the camera server's address, port and device are the phone's own: they stay on the phone, the web's form neither shows nor writes them), `method` (`rings` or `softwareOffset`), `lastAdjustment` (written by the phone only, shown read-only on the web and kept as read: `at`, `star`, `errorArcmin`, `offset` `{xDegrees, yDegrees}`), `exposureSeconds` (1–5), `binning` (1 or 2), `gain`; a guide scope is never an instrument to observe with.

defaultEquipmentItem.description: A row of « Matériel par défaut » as a space reads it: the item shape without `tenantId` and `notes`. A connected telescope's `planner` carries its `group`, `integratedCamera` and `mount`; a default filter's `planner` may carry its `family`.

defaultConfiguration.description: « Ma configuration par défaut » (packages/portal/src/planner/default-configuration.js `normalizeDefaultConfiguration`): the keys of a plan's `equipment` that fill every new plan. A key left out is « à choisir » (never chosen, or an item archived since): a new plan then starts with no telescope, camera or eyepiece chosen (`null`, « Choisir… »), no reducer, no filter and no mount.
